description:
Lowering of two chimney stacks. Lowering of a very high chimney stack on the outside wall due to risk of damage in high winds, and excess weight on outside wall that has had to be pinned due to bowing previously. All other chimney stacks in the road have been lowered previously. 
Lowering of second chimney stack, back of building part of shared wall and so shared chimney stack. Neighbor is in agreement with proposal. This chimney stack is very solid, heavy and we have concerns is causing excessive weight on the back of the property which due to the age of the property would benefit from removal/reduction and it is currently supported by gallows. Both properties have had their chimney breasts removed in the past. . 

The removal / reduction is requested for building safety reasons not cosmetic. 
The chimney stack at the back of the building is decommissioned and supported by Gallows brackets. 

Proposed reduction in height of existing chimney stack - front chimney stack on south facing wall. 
The proposal is to reduce the height of the existing masonry chimney stack while retaining the chimney in its existing position and retaining the existing chimney pots.
The chimney is located on the side elevation of the property and rises from a roof level approximately 7.0 metres above ground level, adjacent to the loft room/roof peak.
The existing masonry chimney stack measures approximately 2,700 mm high × 600 mm wide × 420 mm deep. The two existing chimney pots extend a further 950 mm above the masonry stack, giving a total existing height of approximately 3,650 mm above the roof datum.
It is proposed to reduce the masonry stack to 1,219 mm (4 ft) above the roof datum. The 950 mm chimney pots will be retained, resulting in an overall proposed chimney height of approximately 2,169 mm above the roof datum.
The proposal therefore reduces the overall height of the chimney by approximately 1,481 mm, while retaining its position, width, depth and traditional appearance.
The existing yellow London stock brick will be retained/reused where practicable, with any replacement brickwork and mortar selected to match the existing building.
The submitted drawing  shows:
existing and proposed side elevations;
existing and proposed chimney heights;
the 7.0 m roof-level datum;
the adjacent loft/roof peak;
the 600 mm × 420 mm chimney-stack dimensions;
the 950 mm chimney pots separately from the masonry stack;
chimney-pot plan and elevation details; and
site photographs showing the chimney in the context of the existing property.
The purpose of the works is to reduce the excessive height, weight and prominence of the existing chimney stack whilst retaining the chimney as a characteristic feature of the circa-1860 property.
The property is situated facing west..

The rear chimney stack dimensions are: 1.6 m tall, 1m wide, and 0.8 m deep. Proposed reduction to in line with party wall upstand, 0.3 meters. The chimney would be made good using any retained bricks.
